hooks.text: A violent cosmic impact nearly blasted the Martian moon Phobos into rubble.
A moon survived an impact crater spanning one third of its surface.
How did a tiny Martian moon survive an asteroid impact this colossal?

title: The Asteroid Impact That Nearly Blasted Phobos Apart
description: Stickney crater spans nine kilometers across a moon only twenty-seven kilometers wide. Here is why the ancient cataclysm failed to destroy Phobos.

beats.text: A violent cosmic impact nearly blasted the Martian moon [Phobos](/fˈObˈOz/) into rubble.
beats.visual: Enhanced color HiRISE view of Stickney crater on Phobos, 2008

beats.text: Phobos is an irregular, potato-shaped moon measuring just twenty-seven kilometers across at its widest point.
beats.visual: Viking 1 Orbiter mosaic of the irregular moon Phobos, 1977

beats.text: Carved deep into its fragile face is [Stickney](/stˈɪknˈi/) crater, measuring approximately nine kilometers in diameter.
beats.visual: Mars Express high-resolution view of Stickney crater rim, 2010

beats.text: That single crater covers fully one-third of the tiny moon's entire width.
beats.visual: Close-up of Stickney crater interior slopes from Mars Global Surveyor, 2003

beats.text: An impact of that scale should have completely shattered Phobos into a cloud of debris.
beats.visual: Mariner 9 image showing cratered landscape of Phobos, 1972

beats.text: The moon survived only because its interior is a porous, low-density rubble pile that cushioned the catastrophic shock like a sponge.
beats.visual: Enhanced color HiRISE image showing Phobos rim materials and porosity, 2008

beats.text: Under Phobos's weak gravity, simulations show boulders blasted from Stickney rolled entirely around the moon to carve vast surface grooves.
beats.visual: Detailed view of linear surface grooves on Phobos from Viking orbiter, 1976

beats.text: Today, Mars is pulling Phobos inward, where tidal forces will finish destroying what survived the blast.
beats.visual: Artist concept of tidal gravitational forces disrupting Phobos near Mars, 2015
